title: The asymmetry that flips
question: The asymmetry that flips
hook: All of cryptography rests on checking an answer being cheaper than finding it — AI deployment quietly runs the same asymmetry backwards.
core_idea: Model outputs cost milliseconds and fractions of a cent while verifying one takes scarce human expertise; unverified outputs pile up looking like successes, so systems must be designed so that the check a human CAN afford reveals what matters.
visual_object: a two-pan balance labeled SOLVE / VERIFY that flips over
prerequisites: rough idea of what calling a model costs; P-vs-NP folklore helpful, not required
exclusions: no complexity-theory formalism, no "automate the verification" counterargument beyond one line, no case-study retellings
